firearms.title: Firearms & Ammo
firearms.incompleteBody: This firearm has no {{fields}} recorded. Compliance reads the weapon type and your licenses to work out which activity requirement applies to you, so filling these in may change what the app asks of you. Firearms created by an import usually arrive this way.
firearms.emptyBody: Add a firearm to track rounds fired, maintenance, and license status.
firearms.calibersHint: The chambering is what the firearm is built for, and what your licence names. Below it, add any other cartridge you actually shoot through it — a .357 Magnum revolver fed .38 Special is the usual case, not an odd one. The app never stops you recording an ammunition lot it did not predict.
firearms.ownershipHelp: A firearm you add is taken to be your own. Borrowed covers a club firearm and anyone else's. Owning a handgun is what decides which license-activity requirement the app measures you against.
firearms.maintenanceIntervalHelp: Leave empty to hide the rounds-since indicator.
firearms.groupsHint: The default is the firearm pre-selected when you start a session in that group — one per group, and the same firearm can be the default in several groups.
firearms.sightSettingsHint: Clicks are relative to your own zero — only the difference between settings matters.
firearms.sightLabelPlaceholder: e.g. center hold, six o'clock hold, field center hold
firearms.sightElevationHint: Clicks up from your zero; negative is down. Leave it not recorded if you don't track it.
firearms.sightWindageHint: Clicks right from your zero; negative is left. Leave it not recorded if you don't track it.
firearms.validUntilInvalid: Enter a real date as YYYY-MM-DD, or leave it empty if the license is valid indefinitely.

firearms.scanFromCamera: Take a Photo of the Card
firearms.scanFromLibrary: Choose a Photo of the Card

firearms.scanErrorFailed: The card could not be read. Try again with more light and the card filling the frame.
firearms.scanErrorNothing: No license fields were recognized in that photo.
firearms.scanErrorUnsupported: Card scanning needs the app on a phone; it is not available here.

ammo.emptyBody: Add an ammo lot to link it to sessions and track usage.
ammo.label: Label
ammo.velocityHint: Chronographed muzzle velocity, in meters per second.
ammo.compareOpenSubtitle: See whether one lot actually shoots better than another.
ammo.compareIntro: Ranked by average score per shot. The ranking is not a result on its own — read the sample size and the interval beside each lot before trusting it.
ammo.compareEmptyBody: Link your sessions to an ammo lot and score them. Once two lots have shots behind them, this screen compares them.
ammo.compareThinHint: Fewer than {{count}} scored shots, so this average will still move a lot with every session.
ammo.compareHeadDifference: {{leader}} averages {{delta}} per shot against {{runnerUp}}, and the 95% interval ({{low}} to {{high}}) stays clear of zero — the gap is bigger than the noise.
ammo.compareHeadInconclusive: {{leader}} leads {{runnerUp}} by {{delta}} per shot, but the 95% interval ({{low}} to {{high}}) includes zero. That is not yet a difference you can act on.
ammo.compareHeadInsufficient: Too little data to compare {{leader}} with {{runnerUp}}. Both lots need at least {{count}} scored shots before a difference means anything.
ammo.compareImbalance: These lots differ {{ratio}}x in shot count, so the table is not a fair race — the lot with fewer shots has the less settled average.
ammo.compareCaveats: Shots inside one series move together, so the true uncertainty is a little wider than the intervals shown. And nothing here separates the ammunition from your own form on the day a lot happened to be used.
ammo.mergeConfirmBody_one: Move {{count}} session from “{{duplicate}}” to “{{kept}}” and delete “{{duplicate}}”? Its quantity and notes are not carried over.
ammo.mergeConfirmBody_other: Move {{count}} sessions from “{{duplicate}}” to “{{kept}}” and delete “{{duplicate}}”? Its quantity and notes are not carried over.

settings.locationLookupHelp: When on, what you type in a session’s Location field is sent to photon.komoot.io, and tapping Use My Location sends your coordinates to overpass-api.de.
settings.birthYearRetroactive: You can change it later. Because the veteran class and the gold series thresholds are worked out from it, changing it also changes them for sessions already logged.
settings.birthYearChangeMessage: Change your birth year from {{from}} to {{to}}? The veteran class and the age-reduced gold series thresholds will be recalculated, for sessions already logged as well as new ones.
settings.badgeNoYearNote: No birth year set — showing full-points requirements with no age reduction.
settings.badgeReductionNote: Age reduction of {{points}} p/series applies from {{sinceYear}}.
settings.locationLookupInfo:
Off: only places you have used before are suggested, and nothing leaves your phone.

On: what you type in a session’s Location field is sent to photon.komoot.io, which searches OpenStreetMap. A Use My Location button also appears there; tapping it takes one position fix and sends those coordinates to overpass-api.de to look up shooting ranges near you. Nothing is sent until you tap it, your position is never stored or tracked in the background, and only the range name you pick is saved with the session. You can turn this off again at any time.
settings.badgeInfo:
Points needed per 5-shot precision series for each grade, by weapon group (SHB Bilaga 1 mom 5.1.1.1).

From the year after you turn 55 the requirement drops by 1 point per series, and by 2 points from the year after you turn 65. Set your birth year above to see the table with that reduction applied.
settings.trainingConsent: Keep My Marks as Training Data
settings.trainingHelp: Off by default. Nothing is sent anywhere — the marks stay on this phone.
settings.trainingInfo:
Score from Photo asks you to tap each hole. Automatic detection does not exist yet, and building it needs examples of where holes really are.

When this is on, each series you score from a photo is kept as an example: the positions you tapped, in target millimeters, and which ones you had to nudge. The photo itself is not copied — only a reference to the one already stored with the session.

This never leaves your phone. Nothing is uploaded, nothing is synced, and target photos are personal data. You can turn this off and delete everything collected at any time, without touching your logbook.
settings.trainingDeleteBody: This permanently deletes the {{count}} kept series. Your logbook and photos are not affected.
settings.womensClassesHelp: Offers Dam 1/2/3 alongside your class, and the ISSF events shot by women.
settings.personalSubtitle: Birth year, your class, series requirement
settings.trackingIntro: Switch off what you never record, and its input disappears from the forms. What you have already saved stays, and still shows.
settings.trackHandloadsHint: Off: the ammo form has no handload switch or recipe. A lot that is already a handload keeps them.
settings.trackWeaponGroupsHint: Off: a competition takes its weapon group from the firearm, as training does. It asks only when the firearm fits more than one group.
settings.trackShooterClassHint: Off: a competition records no class, as training does.

session.matchFormatInfo:
The match format decides whether the session arrives laid out as the full match, or empty for you to fill in.

Choose Full Match when you are shooting the format as it is shot in competition. One with a fixed structure lays the series out for you: Military Rapid Fire arrives with a sighter series and twelve scoring series at 10, 8 and 6 seconds. On Precision it is the final that the full match adds.

Choose Free Format when you are shooting the discipline without a fixed format. The series are the discipline's normal length — five shots in precision — and you add them as you go.

timer.title: Timers

fields.timeLimitHint: At no limit the series runs until you stop it, or until the microphone has heard nothing for a while.

timer.cuesHint: Applies to Get Ready, GO and Done. Set your phone to silent to mute the sounds — except while the microphone is listening, when they play anyway.

shots.recordHint: The microphone listens for your shots and records the time to each one. It runs under any of the settings above, so a repetition drill records splits just as a single string does.
shots.sensitivityHint: A shot is counted when it rises this far above the room, does it abruptly, and is over quickly. Higher sensitivity needs less of a rise, so it hears quieter shots and more of everything else. The level it is measured against follows the room, so the setting means the same thing indoors and on a windy range. What it cannot do is tell a shot from another sharp crack — a finger snap counts as a shot at any setting.
shots.liveMeterHint: Clap or dry-fire near the phone. The grey mark is the room, the red one is where the trigger sits above it.
shots.liveMeterNeedsPermission: Grant microphone permission (tap Start once) to see the live level here.
shots.privacyNote: The microphone is analyzed live on this device to find the shots. The recording is never stored, played back or sent anywhere — it is written to a temporary file the app can only meter, and deleted the moment the run ends.
shots.webUnavailable: The shot timer needs a native build — the microphone isn't available in this web preview.

errors.unavailable: No microphone is available on this device.
errors.denied: Microphone permission was denied — allow it in system settings to detect shots.
errors.failed: The microphone couldn't be started. Close other apps using it and try again.

shotDiagnostics.title: Shot Detection Diagnostics
shotDiagnostics.intro: Records what the microphone hears so shot detection can be built from real measurements. Start metering, tap Mark Shot each time you fire, then export the log and send it back.
shotDiagnostics.unitHint: All values in dBFS, where 0 is the loudest the microphone can register. The noise floor follows the room, so "above floor" is how far an event separates from it.
shotDiagnostics.markHint: Tap right after each shot. The marks are what tell a real shot from a door slamming when the log is analyzed.
shotDiagnostics.lastMark_one: Last shot: peak {{peak}} dBFS, {{excess}} dB above the floor, spanning {{count}} sample.
shotDiagnostics.lastMark_other: Last shot: peak {{peak}} dBFS, {{excess}} dB above the floor, spanning {{count}} samples.

modeHint.rangeOfficer: Ladda is called, then you press when the shooters are ready — nothing in between is on a clock. The second press starts the automatic countdown.

faltTimer.laddaTime: Time Between Ladda and Alla klara
faltTimer.partierHint: Whole seconds inside the shooting time — each boundary gives a short beep. The numbers above the timeline are the seconds between boundaries.
faltTimer.cuesHint: Tap to choose how each command reaches you: voice or beep, vibration, or both. Eld upphör can also be a whistle, as the rules allow. At least one stays on.
faltTimer.sourceNote: Commands and timings per SHB 2026 D.6.2 p. 88, on a timeline anchored at Eld (t = 0). Eld upphör is drawn out over the last 3 s so it ends exactly when the shooting time runs out.
faltTimer.scrubHint: Paused — tap the bar or a command to move the clock.

shotlog.title: ShotLog Import
shotlog.intro: Dev tool. Reads ShotLog 5.4’s full export, one row per series with every shot. Each ShotLog session becomes a session with its series and shots. Map the tags, then review every session before importing.

shotlog.tagMappingIntro: ShotLog has no discipline, class or firearm field — it is all in the tags. Change any guess before importing.

regulations.title: Regulations
regulations.intro: The rule sets you compete under. Turning one on adds its disciplines and weapon groups when you create a session; sessions already logged are untouched.
regulations.impliedBy: Already in effect — another regulation you enabled adopts it
regulations.footnote: Svenska Skyttesportförbundet uses the ISSF rulebook for its events, so enabling it brings the ISSF disciplines with it — and adds its own national ones on top: snabbluftpistol, and the open, junior and men's classes shot at SM and DM.
